Playbook.name: Windows — Execution via Microsoft DotNet ClickOnce Host - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Defense Evasion / Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: The ClickOnce host chain fired: rundll32.exe invoked dfshim.dll (ShOpenVerbApplication) — the Microsoft .NET ClickOnce deployment host (dfsvc.exe) — and a network connection followed within 5 seconds under the same user. ClickOnce lets a signed Microsoft binary launch and network-fetch an application from a URL, which adversaries abuse to proxy-execute code and pull a payload while blending in as trusted .NET tooling. The triage question: is this a user launching a legitimate internal ClickOnce app (e.g. a line-of-business deployment), or attacker proxy-execution/ingress via the ClickOnce host?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: On a banking endpoint, ClickOnce proxy-execution can fetch and run attacker code under a trusted signed host, evading application controls and enabling initial access or tooling delivery that looks like normal .NET activity.

Assets.AssetType: Windows workstations and member servers (endpoints running .NET / ClickOnce)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Sysmon process-create (Event ID 1) and network-connect (Event ID 3) shipped to logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: ClickOnce host chain
Signal.Details: rundll32.exe with dfshim + ShOpenVerbApplication, or dfsvc.exe, followed by a network connection within 5s under the same user.id. ClickOnce (dfsvc/dfshim) is a zero-baseline on JCB — any hit is notable.

Input.name: $host
Input.description: Host where the ClickOnce host chain fired (alert host.name).

Input.name: $user
Input.description: User account under which the ClickOnce host ran (alert user.name).

ImmediateCapture.Item: The rundll32/dfsvc command line and its parent process (from the alert).
The destination the follow-on network connection reached.

InitialAssessment.Rule: If the parent is a browser/mail client and the destination is an external/unknown host, lean True Positive (user-initiated ClickOnce ingress).
If the ClickOnce app resolves to a known internal LOB deployment URL and the user routinely runs it, lean False Positive (authorised internal ClickOnce app).

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether the ClickOnce host chain on $host under $user is authorised internal-app execution or attacker proxy-execution / payload ingress.

Step.name: Confirm the ClickOnce host process and read the command line
Step.Purpose: Recover the rundll32/dfsvc ClickOnce host invocation on $host and its parent — the primary TP-vs-FP input.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE host.name == "$host" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND (TO_LOWER(process.name) IN ("rundll32.exe","dfsvc.exe")) AND (TO_LOWER(process.command_line) LIKE "*dfshim*" OR TO_LOWER(process.command_line) LIKE "*shopenverbapplication*" OR TO_LOWER(process.name) == "dfsvc.exe") | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, user.name, process.name, process.executable, process.command_line, process.parent.name, process.parent.executable | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 50

Step.name: Establish the launching context (parent + user)
Step.Purpose: See what launched the ClickOnce host and which users invoke it on $host — a browser/mail parent differs sharply from a scripted/unknown parent.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE host.name == "$host" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND (TO_LOWER(process.name) == "dfsvc.exe" OR (TO_LOWER(process.name) == "rundll32.exe" AND TO_LOWER(process.command_line) LIKE "*dfshim*")) | STATS launches = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY process.parent.name, user.name | SORT launches DESC | LIMIT 20

Step.name: Profile the user's follow-on activity on the host (the payload)
Step.Purpose: ClickOnce pulls and runs an application; profile what $user executed on $host around the event to spot a delivered payload or hands-on tooling.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE host.name == "$host" AND user.name == "$user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS execs = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY process.name, process.parent.name | SORT execs DESC | LIMIT 30

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the ClickOnce host launched from a browser/mail/unknown parent, and INV-03 shows a new/unusual child process or hands-on tooling by $user after it — proxy-execution/ingress via ClickOnce.
Node.Result: True Positive (ClickOnce proxy-execution / payload ingress — begin IR on $host)

Node.Condition: The ClickOnce app maps to a documented internal LOB deployment routinely run by $user, parent is Explorer/a known launcher, and no anomalous follow-on — authorised internal ClickOnce app; OR the network fetch was positively proven blocked at the proxy/firewall (record as blocked, never "benign").
Node.Result: False Positive (authorised internal ClickOnce app OR proven-blocked fetch — record which)

Node.Condition: A legitimate but un-baselined internal ClickOnce deployment is triggering the rule for many users.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (baseline the internal ClickOnce URL/app; add a scoped exception)

Node.Condition: The launching parent, the ClickOnce URL, or the follow-on cannot be recovered from telemetry, so intent is unclear.

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised internal ClickOnce line-of-business application, or a ClickOnce fetch positively proven blocked. Not "benign" — record which.

Indicators.Item: ClickOnce URL/app is a documented internal deployment; $user runs it routinely; parent is Explorer/known launcher.
The follow-on network connection was denied at the proxy/firewall.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the internal ClickOnce app owner/URL; propose a scoped exception for that app.
If blocked, document the blocked fetch, preserve evidence, close as false_positive (blocked).

TruePositive.Definition: ClickOnce host was used to proxy-execute code and/or fetch a payload from an untrusted source.

Indicators.Item: Browser/mail/unknown parent; external or unknown destination.
New/unusual child process or hands-on tooling by $user after the event.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate $host; capture the ClickOnce URL and any fetched artifact; hunt for persistence and lateral movement from $user/$host.
Reset $user credentials if compromise is confirmed; open an incident.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Recover the ClickOnce command line, parent, and destination (INV-01/02); if the parent/destination is untrusted, queue $host for isolation.
Identify and preserve any application/artifact fetched by the ClickOnce host.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate $host, remove the fetched payload and any persistence, and block the ingress URL/destination at the proxy.
Reset $user credentials if hands-on compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Baseline/allow-list authorised internal ClickOnce deployments; restrict ClickOnce to known internal URLs via policy; alert on ClickOnce host reaching external destinations.

Escalation.Trigger: Untrusted parent/destination, a delivered payload, hands-on follow-on, or a server/privileged host involved.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: ClickOnce tied to a documented internal app (or fetch proven blocked); no anomalous follow-on; exception scoped if needed.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: $host isolated, payload/persistence removed, ingress destination blocked, credentials reset, incident documented with INV-01/02/03 evidence.
